title: It is written (Matthew 4:1–11)
hookLine: each answer to the tempter comes from Deuteronomy
tomorrow: where does a light start, if not in the capital?

cards: Late, the house asleep, and the thought sounds very reasonable: one more, you deserve it, nobody will know. Temptation doesn't have to sound like a villain. It can even quote scripture.
Right after the river, Matthew says, the Spirit led Jesus into the wilderness "to be tempted of the devil." Forty days without food, and afterward he was hungry.
Then: "If thou be the Son of God, command that these stones be made bread."

teach.b: Three tests, and every answer starts the same way. Bread first: "It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God."
Then the tempter sets him on a pinnacle of the temple and quotes scripture himself, a psalm promising angels will catch you so you won't dash your foot against a stone. Go on, jump.
Jesus: "It is written again, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God."
Then a high mountain, all the kingdoms of the world, offered for one act of worship. "Get thee hence, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve."

All three answers come from one book, Deuteronomy, Moses' words to Israel in the wilderness, where God let the people hunger and fed them manna, so they'd learn that "man doth not live by bread only."
Now the part that matters on an ordinary Tuesday night. Jesus never argues with the tempter's logic, and he never improvises something clever.

It is written isn't a password, either. The devil quotes scripture too. What holds is a line already lived with, there before the pull arrives, the way Jesus answered a wilderness with Israel's own wilderness lessons.

how: Some churches read the temptation in the wilderness at the start of Lent, a season of fasting and self-denial, and some Christians memorize short verses to say when temptation comes.

an answer from scripture, already learned
a rule that can never be changed at all

games.q: it is written — tap the pairs.
p: thou shalt not tempt the Lord

s: the devil never quotes scripture in the story
on the pinnacle of the temple he quotes a psalm about angels catching you.
all three of Jesus' answers come from Deuteronomy
bread alone, do not tempt the Lord, and worship God only: each is from Moses' words to Israel.
the forty days without food come from later tradition, not Matthew
Matthew 4:2 says it: forty days and forty nights, and afterward he was hungry.

games.q: your group chat dares you to post something cruel about a classmate. someone adds, "come on, it's just a joke." what would answering like Jesus look like?
o: answer with a line you already hold, and don't post.
out-argue them with a clever comeback first.
post it, then apologize later with a verse.
games.why: Jesus didn't debate the tempter's logic. three times he answered: it is written, with a line he already lived by.

practice: Pick one short line that answers a pull you know well: man shall not live by bread alone, or a line from a source you trust. Say it out loud, slowly, five times, until it starts to stay, and then let it ride quietly on the breath.

wordCard.voice: It is written. Jesus' answer to the tempter, three times over, each one a line from Deuteronomy.

orig.note: Greek: it is written, it stands written. Jesus' word to the tempter in Matthew 4:4.

carryVoice: Your line: it is written. The tempter knew the words too; Jesus lived by them. Take care.
